```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
```

# Data

The data are the Bank Marketing dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository
(Moro, Cortez & Rita, 2014): telephone marketing campaigns run by a Portuguese bank between
May 2008 and November 2010. Put `bank-additional-full.csv` in the same folder as this `.Rmd`.

The file uses semicolons, not commas, to separate columns (a common European convention,
because the comma is used as the decimal mark), so it is read with `read_delim(delim = ";")`.

```{r read-data}
bank_raw <- read_delim("bank-additional-full.csv", delim = ";")
glimpse(bank_raw)
count(bank_raw, month)
count(bank_raw, y)
```

## Data dictionary

```{r data-dictionary}
data_dictionary <- tribble(
  ~variable, ~description,
  "y",     "Whether the client subscribed to a term deposit (\"yes\" or \"no\")",
  "month", "Month of the last contact with the client (\"mar\" to \"dec\"; the year is not recorded)"
)
kable(data_dictionary, col.names = c("Variable", "Description"))
```

```{r tidy-data}
bank <- bank_raw |>
  transmute(
    subscribed = as.integer(y == "yes"),
    month = factor(month, levels = c("mar", "apr", "may", "jun", "jul",
                                     "aug", "sep", "oct", "nov", "dec"))
  )
glimpse(bank)
```

# Proportion subscribing and number contacted in each month

```{r overall}
# Overall proportion subscribing (reported in the write-up)
bank |> summarise(n = n(), subscribed = sum(subscribed), prop = mean(subscribed))
```

```{r month-summary}
month_summary <- bank |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarise(n = n(), prop = mean(subscribed)) |>
  mutate(share_of_contacts = n / sum(n))

kable(month_summary, digits = 3)
```

There are no contacts in January or February, so those months are missing.

```{r small-months}
# Share of all contacts in the four months with the highest subscription rates
month_summary |>
  filter(month %in% c("mar", "sep", "oct", "dec")) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), share_of_contacts = sum(share_of_contacts))
```

# Logistic regression

March is the first level of `month`, so it is the reference month. The model is

$$\log\left(\frac{p_i}{1-p_i}\right) = \beta_0 + \beta_1\,\text{apr}_i + \beta_2\,\text{may}_i + \beta_3\,\text{jun}_i + \beta_4\,\text{jul}_i + \beta_5\,\text{aug}_i + \beta_6\,\text{sep}_i + \beta_7\,\text{oct}_i + \beta_8\,\text{nov}_i + \beta_9\,\text{dec}_i$$

where $p_i$ is the probability that person $i$ subscribed, $\text{apr}_i$ to $\text{dec}_i$ are
dummy variables equal to 1 if person $i$ was last contacted in that month and 0 otherwise,
$\beta_0$ is the log odds of subscribing in March, and $\beta_1$ to $\beta_9$ are the differences
in log odds between each month and March.

```{r model}
m1 <- glm(subscribed ~ month, family = binomial, data = bank)
summary(m1)
```

## Does the proportion subscribing differ between months?

A likelihood ratio test compares the model with month to a model with only an intercept
(the same probability in every month).

```{r lrt}
m0 <- glm(subscribed ~ 1, family = binomial, data = bank)
anova(m0, m1, test = "Chisq")
```

# Predicted probabilities with 95% CIs

The confidence intervals are calculated on the log odds scale and then converted to
probabilities, so they stay between 0 and 1.

```{r predictions}
pred_df <- tibble(month = factor(levels(bank$month), levels = levels(bank$month)))

pred <- predict(m1, newdata = pred_df, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)

pred_df <- pred_df |>
  mutate(
    log_odds = pred$fit,
    se       = pred$se.fit,
    p        = plogis(log_odds),
    lo       = plogis(log_odds - 1.96 * se),
    hi       = plogis(log_odds + 1.96 * se)
  )

kable(pred_df, digits = 3)
```

```{r fig1}
p_pred <- ggplot(pred_df, aes(x = month, y = p)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = str_to_title) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 0.6)) +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = "Probability of subscribing",
       title = "Predicted probability of subscribing, by month",
       subtitle = "Points are model predictions; bars are 95% confidence intervals") +
  theme_minimal()

p_pred
ggsave("fig1_predicted_probabilities.png", p_pred, width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 300)
```

# The odds of a subscription in September

```{r sep-odds}
sep <- pred_df |> filter(month == "sep")
sep_odds <- sep$p / (1 - sep$p)
sep_odds
```

The odds are about 0.82: in September, roughly four people subscribed for every five who did not.
This is not a probability; the probability of subscribing in September was about 45%.

## By hand from the coefficients

```{r sep-by-hand}
b <- coef(m1)
sep_log_odds_hand <- b["(Intercept)"] + b["monthsep"]           # 1. log odds
sep_odds_hand     <- exp(sep_log_odds_hand)                      # 2. odds
sep_p_hand        <- sep_odds_hand / (1 + sep_odds_hand)         # 3. probability

c(log_odds = sep_log_odds_hand, odds = sep_odds_hand, p = sep_p_hand)
sep   # matches the model predictions
```

# Why does the proportion subscribing vary over months?

```{r fig2}
p_why <- ggplot(month_summary, aes(x = n, y = prop)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), colour = "#2C7FB8", alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = str_to_title(month)), vjust = -1.2, size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 0.6)) +
  labs(x = "People contacted in the month (log scale)",
       y = "Proportion subscribing",
       title = "Months with fewer contacts had higher subscription rates") +
  theme_minimal()

p_why
ggsave("fig2_contacts_vs_subscription.png", p_why, width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```

Months in which the bank contacted fewer people had higher subscription rates. This is an
association: these data cannot show why. The year of each contact is not recorded, so months may
also differ in, for example, economic conditions during 2008 to 2010.
